Our findings suggest that the spherical multipoles provide the most accurate description of electromagnetic scattering behavior, as demonstrated with an example of an amorphous silicon sphere. These multipoles are utilized to model the optical force exerted on particles composed of semiconductors, dielectrics, and metals over a broad range of wavelengths. Contrasting results highlight the necessity of a comprehensive electromagnetic description. Our analysis emphasizes the importance of selecting the most suitable multipoles to model optical forces effectively. We also examine the influence of particle size on the applicability of the multipoles. For larger particles, where the wavelength of light is comparable to the particle size, the scattering behavior is largely determined by higher-order multipoles. This study introduces two categories of elements in the algebra U(gl(n)), specifically double Young-Capelli bitableaux and central Schur elements, both displaying remarkable action on the highest weight vectors of irreducible Schur modules. The central Schur elements can be viewed as a sum of double Young-Capelli bitableaux corresponding to various strictly increasing Young tableaux. These elements equate to preimages under the Harish-Chandra isomorphism of shifted Schur polynomials, aligning with quantum immanants as per Okounkov. Notably, the representation of Schur elements/quantum immanants bypasses reliance on irreducible characters of symmetric groups. Column and row Schur elements correspond to Capelli and Nazarov-Umeda elements, with duality within these categories stemming from dual combinatorial descriptions of their eigenvalues. Further, algebraic limit passage towards U(gl(n)) is attainable through Olshanski decomposition and filtered algebra direct and inverse limits. As such, analogues of these elements exist within U(gl(n)), realising quantum immanants as limits of their predecessors. In the process, this study generalises, simplifies and clarifies existing theories, incorporating novel algebraic techniques. These findings pave the way for exploring representation theory of quantum groups through quantum immanants and their central counterparts. Lastly, this study outlines potential applications to non-interacting fermionic systems and shifted shifted poset models. Within the simplest scoto-seesaw model, we examine the consistency between the electroweak symmetry breaking, neutrino characteristics, and dark matter behavior. By integrating the minimal dark sector into the simplest "missing partner" type-I seesaw model, we establish a comprehensive understanding of neutrino oscillation lengths. Here, the "atmospheric" mass scale is directly produced at tree level, whereas the "solar" scale arises through radiative processes. Furthermore, we determine the parameter ranges that meet theoretical requirements, in addition to dark matter criteria, including its connection to the cold dark matter density composition. Utilizing two-loop renormalization group equations, we assess the stability of the vacuum and verify the consistency of the Higgs boson's properties with experimental data. Moreover, we investigate the prospects for direct and indirect dark matter detection, as well as neutrino-related experiments within this framework. Several novel features of this model include: (1) neutrino oscillation length predictions; (2) the derivation of the dark matter particle's mass range; (3) the scalar sector's influence on neutrinoless double beta decay; (4) the dark matter particle's participation in neutrino-related processes; and (5) the potential for detecting this model through dark matter or neutrino-related experiments. By exploring this simplest scoto-seesaw model, we can identify potential clues for distinguishing it from other neutrino-driven dark matter models in the near future.

We employ exact diagonalization to examine the effects of spin-orbit coupling and electron-electron interactions on the mixing of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ $d$-orbital states in a cubic crystal structure, characteristic of certain transition metal oxides. By directly comparing with $t_{2g}$ only or $e_g$ only models based on electron filling, we investigate the magnetic properties of all possible $d$-shell configurations, incorporating calculations of the total magnetic moment, orbital occupation, and effective spin-orbit coupling. The resulting parameters are expressed in terms of interaction strength and spin-orbit coupling, and a phase diagram is constructed to illustrate the resulting magnetic moments. The orbital occupation is found to exhibit a more complex pattern, influenced by both on-site interactions and spin-orbit coupling, and can result in the occupation of $e_g$ states in the $t_{2g}$ only series and vice versa. The relevance of this study to experimental observations, specifically branching ratio ratios in Raman spectra, is also considered, and we suggest that significant mixing between $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ states may provide an alternative explanation for certain experimental findings. To facilitate further investigation, we propose possible research paths involving theoretical modeling of Raman spectra based on our findings. Additionally, we suggest possible experimental verification of our results through resonant soft X-ray scattering and Raman spectroscopy in systems like Sr$_3$Ti$_2$O$_7$ and LaTiO$_3$. The mixing of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ states is found to result in significant changes to the electronic structure and associated excitations, and not just minor adjustments as has been a common assumption in the past. The implications of this discovery are far-reaching and will require a revision of current understanding in various areas including superconductivity and magnetism in transition metal oxides. This research examines how relative quantum cohomology evolves under certain mathematical transformations known as birational transformations. Specifically, it investigates the properties of relative I-functions in the context of toric complete intersections. For a particular type of toric complete intersections with specified divisor properties, it shows that the relative I-functions can be matched directly. Additionally, it demonstrates that the relative I-functions for another class of toric complete intersections can be connected through analytical means. Furthermore, it explores connections between these results and the related mathematical theories of extremal transitions and FJRW.

Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. advanced analysis. It is capable of handling object-feature tables that include
numerical values and text-based labels for objects and features. The tool
encompasses several statistical techniques such as weighted PCA, elastic maps,

K-Means clustering and multilinear regression. With customizable visualizations
and an interactive 3D viewer, ViDaExpert enables the creation of 3D scenes
from data and facilitates rapid, in-depth analysis of data, encompassing
elementary to complex methodologies. The software is part of the MAIA project
and was created to support the development of multimedia contents for didactic
purposes, specifically designed to be employed in an educational environment
